slides.texte_overlay:
How to master the art of
a first impression
Smell clean, not strong. Fresh clothes, a light scent, clean breath. People notice smell before they notice almost anything else, and it shapes their first feeling about you.
Say their name back right away. "Nice to meet you, Daniel." Repeating the name helps you remember it and shows you were paying attention from the first second.
Have a warm one-line answer to "What do you do?" Not just a job title. "I help small restaurants get more customers." A short story is more memorable than a label.
Show interest with your body. Lean in slightly, nod, keep your hands relaxed. People feel your attention long before they hear any of your words.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Having interesting things to say makes every first meeting easier and more memorable.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Interesting things to say make first meetings easier.

slides.texte_overlay: Find one thing in common quickly. Same city, same sport, same favourite food. Shared ground turns a stranger into someone who feels familiar within minutes.
Finish with a clear, friendly goodbye. "Really nice meeting you, enjoy the rest of the evening." The last few seconds are remembered almost as much as the first.
